rule_set.name: autosys-integration-classes
rule_set.provenance: Vendor documentation + the 4427-job public sample; no customer data
rule_set.notes: Prototype for the assessment report classifier. One primary class per job, traits are orthogonal flags. No rule names a customer, host or job. v0.1.1: 6 ambiguous any-scope tokens split to exe-scoped sibling rules (jil, chase, forecast, oc, helm, bq, cmd, sh, isql) after finding they misclassify a plain command whose destination argument happens to share the name, while building T15. Long/distinctive vendor binary names (mysqldump, spark-submit, etc.) were checked and left at any scope: coincidental collision with those is not a realistic risk the way it is for a short word.

file_trigger.label: File trigger (FT job type, distinct from file watcher and FTP)

rules.notes: FT is File Trigger per vendor docs - NOT an alias of FTP
JIL 'job_type: ps' aliases to PEOPLESOFT
insert_job_type site-defined types land here; declared name kept as evidence
AE command binaries; any token (a wrapper calling sendevent is still coupled)
TWS/HCL binaries; 'composer'/'maestro' are common words so scope=exe
ESP commands run inside ESP JCL; token hits in AutoSys commands suggest a bridge - needs review
auto_r3* are legacy CA/Broadcom SAP Adapter binaries; KB names sibling binary sapjob. Vendor claim.
SAP kernel/RFC tools; 'tp' (transport) deliberately excluded - too ambiguous
Legacy AutoSys PeopleSoft Adapter binaries (auto_ps7 etc.)
Name-inferred wrapper: executable contains informatica/infa tokens. Review with customer.
SECONDARY SOURCE - Ab Initio docs are not public. Vendor docs live behind their support portal.
m_ls/m_cp/m_eval utilities; medium-low because m_* names collide
exp/imp are 3-letter words; only trusted as the executable itself

isql exists in Sybase Adaptive Server, unixODBC and older MSSQL - vendor cannot be told from the token alone Rescoped to exe while building T15: 'isql' is short enough to collide with an ordinary bare argument.
Both products retired to the Apache Attic (Sqoop 2021, Oozie 2025) - class doubles as a redesign flag
'az' is a very short token; exe scope only, medium confidence
Unidentified ftp-named binary (e.g. a site MFT wrapper). Class is right; vendor is unknown.
IBM Sterling Connect:Direct; 'direct' is an English word - exe scope only
MFT tool name heuristics - no public CLI doc to cite; review with customer
'mail' alone is a common word - exe scope, medium confidence
Reachability probes; 'ping'/'nc' are mid-command words too - exe scope only
Windows-only utilities without an extension in the command
'sh' bare token as interpreter call
Catch-all for single-utility commands; composite scripts land in unix_script
Test/placeholder commands; medium because echo is also used inside real scripts

traits.label: inline-credential-shape
traits.notes: Generic kv/uri shapes only - short -p/-w flags need exe context and are handled by the fixed redactor layer

traits.label: talend-name-shape
traits.notes: Talend jobs look like <job>_run.<ext>; name alone is too weak to be a class so it is a review hint

traits.label: credential-via-scriptfile
traits.notes: ftp -s:file and winscp /script move secrets out of the command but into a file

traits.label: windows-env-var-shape
traits.notes: %VAR% or %%VAR%% are cmd environment references, NOT AutoSys $$ globals - separate trait

traits.label: placeholder-command
traits.notes: literal <...> template text - unparseable placeholder, not a real command

traits.label: autosys-name-hint
traits.notes: command mentions autosys by name - scheduler coupling hint for review, not a class

unclassified.behavior: Never scores XS/trivial. Printed as its own line in the report with the matched evidence field empty; the top executable basenames of the unclassified set are listed for customer review.
